I understand you want to test branching from the root of a repository or version control system.

Here’s how you can do that in **Git**, which is the most common version control system:

## Creating a branch directly from the root commit

If you want to branch from the **very first commit** (root commit):

```bash
# Find the root commit hash
git rev-list --max-parents=0 HEAD

# Create a branch from that root commit
git branch <branch-name> <root-commit-hash>

# Or create and switch to it
git checkout -b <branch-name> <root-commit-hash>
```

## Create a branch from the current root/top of the tree

If you meant **branching from the current HEAD** (main/trunk):

```bash
# Create a branch at your current position
git branch <new-branch-name>

# Or create and switch to it
git checkout -b <new-branch-name>

# With Git 2.23+, you can also use:
git switch -c <new-branch-name>
```

## Example workflow

```bash
# Check current branch
git branch

# Create a branch from root commit
git checkout -b experiment-from-root $(git rev-list --max-parents=0 HEAD)

# Verify you're on the new branch
git log --oneline
```
